source_caption_text:
Parkway Gardens Had Quite The Surprise this morning as federal agents raided the area 

A complex better known worldwide as O’Block — is a historic residential community on Chicago’s South Side, along King Drive. Originally developed in the 1950s as affordable cooperative housing for Black families, Parkway Gardens became an important part of the city’s history during the Great Migration. 

Over time, economic disinvestment, poverty, gang conflict and violence shaped the neighborhood’s reputation, while the community itself remained home to generations of families.

O’Block later became internationally recognized through Chicago’s drill music scene, with artists such as King Von, Chief Keef and Fredo Santana closely associated with the area. Its story is therefore a complicated one—one involving Black history, family, community, hardship, violence and music.
